analysis:
Reviewed the supplied units: .github/workflows/ci.yml (head text only, lines 1-817; no base diff supplied, so the specific changed lines are not identifiable) and .github/workflows/integration.yml (patch hunks at about lines 287-350 plus a metadata-only unit). No coordinator, provider or crypto source changes were visible, so no runtime trust-boundary behavior changes were found.

integration.yml: the paged-KV gate now sets DARKBLOOM_CBV2_KV_QUANTIZATION=native and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_CHECKPOINT_QUANTIZATION=native. The default-posture smoke lane now fails if either variable is set, expects backend 'auto' instead of 'contiguous', and relies on provider defaults of native inference and balanced checkpoints. This only changes test posture. It is CI-only and does not affect production prefix-cache scope, TTL, HMAC lookup naming or the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch tracked in T-041/SEC-035. The weakened assertion (auto instead of contiguous) reduces regression detection and is not a security regression.

ci.yml: actions are pinned by SHA, except the actions/cache/restore and actions/cache/save usages in test-provider at about lines 385 and 396, which are pinned by SHA without a version comment; this is unchanged supply-chain hygiene. There are no pull_request_target triggers, no secrets, and permissions are limited to contents: read on the changes job. The provider-test-gate enforces selected-lane results. The threat-model review scripts are only tested against local fixtures. Release/R2 supply chain is out of scope.

No findings. Later passes should check whether changed Swift or coordinator sources actually default native KV and checkpoint quantization, which would bear on T-041 disk and at-rest posture; this was not visible here.
